scenes.say: Meet Dex. He works in the world's busiest mail room. And today, a thousand questions just landed on his desk.
Is this email a complaint? Which team gets it? How urgent is it? Every single answer is needed right now.
Most AIs reply with a paragraph. Every time. And your code has to read every one of them.
Then Google hands Dex a new tool. The Gemini Decisions API. It doesn't write. It decides.
Yes or no. Pick one. Or score it. One input, up to a thousand questions, in one call.
Google says the whole job takes about a quarter of a second. And it costs ten cents per million input tokens.
But here's the plot twist. Every benchmark number comes from Google itself. And a rival called Jev wins two of the nine tests.
So who is it for? Teams making the same small decision, thousands of times a day. It reads audio, video and PDFs. But it isn't the cheapest, you can't self-host it, and it can't write.
Full pros and cons, with sources, are on my blog. Follow, and Dex and I will be back tomorrow with another AI tool.
